rationale: Each 3x3 block becomes its most common colour including zero: five ones beat four zeros in demonstration 1, while four twos lose to five zeros in demonstration 2.
Each vertical pair becomes 5 if either cell is nonzero, otherwise 0; demonstration 2 maps the pair [0,1] to 5.
Each 3x3 block returns its most common nonzero colour, or 0 when empty; demonstration 1 returns 3 from the bottom-right block containing four threes and five zeros.
Each 2x2 block returns its most common colour including zero; three ones produce 1 in demonstration 1, while two twos tied with two zeros produce 0 in demonstration 3.
Each horizontal pair returns 5 when any cell is nonzero and 0 when both are zero; demonstration 2 maps [3,0] to 5.
Each vertical pair returns its most common nonzero colour, or 0 if empty; demonstration 2 maps [0,1] to 1 and demonstration 3 maps [0,2] to 2.
Each 2x2 block becomes 5 if any nonzero cell occurs, otherwise 0; demonstration 1 includes a block with one three that outputs 5 and an empty block that outputs 0.
Each 2x2 block returns its most common nonzero colour, or 0 when empty; demonstration 2 maps two twos with two zeros to 2, and demonstration 3 similarly preserves sparse threes.
Each 2x3 block returns its most common colour including zero; demonstration 1 maps three twos tied with three zeros to 0, while four twos with two zeros produce 2.
